topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its main learning outcomes regarding cancer treatments.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the principles, modes of action, clinical examples, side effects, and resistance mechanisms of traditional cancer treatments.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic vulnerabilities, checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that capitalize on specific tumor vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and synthetic lethality in DNA repair.

topics.label: Oncogene targeting, kinase inhibitors, and mechanisms of drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the design of targeted kinase inhibitors against driver oncogenes and examine the cellular mechanisms and clinical management of treatment resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the therapeutic use of engineered antibodies to directly inhibit surface receptors, induce cytotoxic immune responses, or deliver linked toxins to tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell engineering
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the immune system interacts with tumors and detail therapeutic strategies to harness or genetically redirect T cells against cancer.

topics.label: Clinical challenges, long-term progress, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the major clinical hurdles, historical survival trends, emerging management paradigms, and ethical dilemmas in modern oncology.
